system_overview: This specification is a model-checking configuration for the Dijkstra-Scholten termination detection algorithm (EWD687a). It instantiates the abstract algorithm with a specific small network of four processes and five directed edges, enabling finite-state model checking with TLC to verify the algorithm's correctness properties.
actors_and_components: The system consists of four processes: a leader and three additional processes. The network topology is defined as a specific set of directed edges connecting these processes, with the leader having only outgoing edges as required by the algorithm.
state_variables: All state variables are inherited from the base EWD687a specification: activity status for each process, sent-unacknowledged and received-unacknowledged counters for each edge, overlay tree parent edges, in-transit computation messages, and in-transit acknowledgment messages.
initial_state: The initial state follows the base specification: only the leader is active, all message and acknowledgment counters are zero, and no process has a parent in the overlay tree.
actions: All actions are inherited from the base EWD687a specification: sending computation messages, receiving acknowledgments, sending acknowledgments (with overlay tree management), receiving computation messages, and processes becoming idle.
safety_properties: The model-checking configuration inherits all safety properties from the base specification, including the main safety property that leader neutrality implies global neutrality.
model_bounds: The system is bounded to four processes with five directed edges. A state constraint limits message, acknowledgment, sent-unacknowledged, and received-unacknowledged counters on each edge to be less than three, keeping the state space finite for exhaustive model checking.
additional_assumptions: The specific network topology includes duplicate edges (which are collapsed to a single edge due to set semantics). The edge set includes bidirectional connections between some process pairs, allowing both computation messages and acknowledgments to flow.
